problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}15yx\,\text{d}V
$$

where $R$ is the type III region given by 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 2-x,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}.
$$
worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}15xy\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}15xy\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}15xy\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}15xy\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}15x{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}dz\,dx \\  & =\frac{15}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}x(4-{x}^{2})\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{15}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}x(4-{x}^{2})\,dz\,dx & =\frac{15}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2-x}x(4-{x}^{2})\,dz]dx \\  & =\frac{15}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}x(4-{x}^{2})[z]_{z=0}^{z=2-x}\,dx \\  & =\frac{15}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}x(4-{x}^{2})(2-x)dx \\  & =\frac{15}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(8x-4{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}+{x}^{4})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{15}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(8x-4{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}+{x}^{4})\,dx & ={[30{x}^{2}-10{x}^{3}-\frac{15{x}^{4}}{4}+\frac{3{x}^{5}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =28.\end{aligned}
$$
